how.title: How it works
how.subtitle: Three steps. No account, no cloud, no middleman.

steps.title: Connect your key
steps.desc: Paste your own OpenAI API key. CloakView talks directly to OpenAI — never through our servers, because we don't have any.

steps.title: It listens
steps.desc: During the call, CloakView transcribes the conversation locally on your Mac and detects when it's your turn to speak.

steps.title: It suggests
steps.desc: A private overlay shows context-aware replies. Only you see them; the overlay never touches the call itself.

features.title: Built for privacy, not for lock-in
features.subtitle: Every design decision favors your control.

items.title: Private overlay
items.desc: Suggestions render on your screen only — invisible to Zoom, Meet, Teams and everyone else on the call.

items.title: Local-first
items.desc: No accounts, no telemetry, no backend. Your meeting data never leaves your Mac.

items.title: BYOK-first
items.desc: Bring your own OpenAI key. We never resell API access and we never mark it up.

items.title: Global shortcuts
items.desc: Summon or hide the overlay from any app with a keystroke you choose.

items.title: English & Spanish
items.desc: The app and this site are fully bilingual. Transcription and suggestions handle both languages.

items.title: No bot in the call
items.desc: CloakView captures system audio on your Mac. No plugin to install, no bot joining your meeting.

costs.title: Honest costs
costs.body: CloakView is free in v1. You pay your own OpenAI API consumption — typically a few dollars a month for regular use — directly to OpenAI at their listed rates. We take nothing: no subscription, no markup, no cut.
points: OpenAI bills you at their public rates — we never touch your money
Revoke the key anytime and the app simply stops

items.q: Are you listening to me?
items.a: No. Audio is processed on your Mac and sent to OpenAI only to transcribe and suggest, using your own key. We operate no servers, so there is nowhere for us to listen from.

items.q: Where do the transcripts go?
items.a: Transcripts stay on your Mac. They are never uploaded to a CloakView server because no such server exists. You can review and delete them at any time.

items.q: Why should I hand my OpenAI key to an unknown app?
items.a: You shouldn't hand it to anyone — that's the point. Your key is stored in the macOS Keychain on your machine and is sent only to OpenAI's API. You can revoke it from the OpenAI dashboard at any moment.

items.q: What happens if I revoke the key?
items.a: CloakView stops working until you add a new one. Nothing breaks, nothing is lost, and we are never notified.

items.q: Does it work with Teams?
items.a: Yes. CloakView works alongside Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams on macOS 14.2+. Because it captures system audio locally, it needs no plugin and no bot joining your call.

items.q: Does the app connect to any server of yours?
items.a: We don't have servers. The only network traffic is between your Mac and OpenAI's API — something you can verify with any traffic inspector.

items.q: What if OpenAI's API goes down mid-meeting?
items.a: The overlay pauses and tells you, instead of pretending everything is fine. Transcription and suggestions resume when the API recovers.

items.q: Isn't using this cheating?
items.a: That's your call to make, like using notes or a colleague's whisper in the room. CloakView is a tool; what you do with it is your responsibility.

faq.intro: Clear answers before you install. The app and GitHub repository have not been published yet.

items.q: Does CloakView record or upload meetings to its own servers?
items.a: No CloakView backend or telemetry is planned. Meeting audio is processed on your Mac and API requests go directly to OpenAI with your key. Check OpenAI’s data handling policy before using the service.

items.q: Where is my API key stored?
items.a: The planned app stores your key in macOS Keychain and sends it directly to OpenAI, not to CloakView servers. Revoke it in your OpenAI account whenever you like.

items.q: Can other people on the call see the overlay?
items.a: The overlay is designed to appear only on your Mac. Test your screen-sharing setup before a sensitive meeting: sharing your entire screen may expose anything visible on it.

items.q: Should I include my key or meeting audio in a support report?
items.a: No. Never send API keys, raw audio, transcripts, or private meeting details in a support email or public issue.

items.q: When can I download the app?
items.a: Not yet. The repository and signed release artifacts are pending; this site will link to the official release when it exists.

items.q: Which macOS version do I need?
items.a: macOS 14.2 or later is planned. Check the release notes for the final system requirements before installing.

items.q: What if macOS blocks the installer?
items.a: Verify the official signed and notarized release. Do not bypass Gatekeeper or remove quarantine flags to force an unverified copy to run.

items.q: Is CloakView free?
items.a: The planned v1 is free, with no CloakView subscription. You pay your own OpenAI API usage directly to OpenAI.

items.q: Does a ChatGPT subscription cover API usage?
items.a: No. OpenAI API billing is separate from a ChatGPT subscription. Set a usage limit in your OpenAI account.

items.q: Can I stop API charges?
items.a: Stop using the app and revoke your API key in your OpenAI dashboard. Check your OpenAI billing page for any outstanding usage.

items.q: Does it work with Zoom, Meet and Teams?
items.a: It is designed to work alongside Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams on a supported Mac, without adding a bot to the call. Actual support should be confirmed when the app ships.

items.q: Is there a Windows version?
items.a: No Windows build is planned for v1. The download page will show the availability of each platform.

items.q: Are Apple Silicon and Intel supported?
items.a: Both are planned; Intel and Apple Silicon artifacts are not yet published. Only install an official release matched to your Mac.

items.q: Why can’t it hear the meeting?
items.a: Check Screen & System Audio Recording permission, the meeting app’s output device and whether listening is enabled. Restart the app after changing permissions.

items.q: Why can’t it hear my voice?
items.a: Check Microphone permission and the selected input device in macOS settings, then try again.

items.q: What happens when OpenAI is unavailable?
items.a: Suggestions require OpenAI connectivity. Check your key, billing, network connection and OpenAI service status; the planned app should not pretend requests succeeded.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: How CloakView handles your data: local-first, no backend, no accounts, no telemetry.
privacy.jurisdiction: Governed by the laws of Florida, USA.

overview.title: Overview
overview.content: CloakView is built on a simple principle: your data stays yours. We operate no backend, maintain no accounts, and collect no telemetry. This policy explains what happens to your information when you use CloakView.

dataCollection.title: What Data We Collect
dataCollection.content:
CloakView does not collect, store, or transmit any user data to CloakView servers. Specifically:

• We do not collect meeting audio, transcripts, or personal information.
• We do not create accounts or user profiles.
• We do not use cookies, tracking pixels, or analytics.
• We do not log your API usage or meeting details.

The only data transmitted outside your Mac is to OpenAI's API, using your own API key, for the purpose of transcription and suggestion generation.

openaiProcessing.title: OpenAI API Usage
openaiProcessing.content:
When you use CloakView with your OpenAI API key:

• Your meeting audio is sent to OpenAI's API servers to be transcribed.
• Context is sent to OpenAI to generate suggestions.
• You are responsible for reviewing OpenAI's privacy policy at openai.com/privacy.
• CloakView never stores, logs, or monitors these requests.
• OpenAI's terms require that you own the rights to the audio being sent. You remain responsible for compliance.

No data is retained by CloakView beyond the session.

yourKey.title: Your API Key
yourKey.content:
Your OpenAI API key is:

• Stored locally in macOS Keychain on your Mac only.
• Never sent to CloakView servers (we do not have any).
• Sent only to OpenAI's API when you use CloakView.
• Your responsibility to protect. Do not share it or include it in support reports.
• Revocable immediately in your OpenAI dashboard.

We never see, log, or monitor your key in any way.

tracking.title: No Tracking or Analytics
tracking.content: CloakView does not include analytics, telemetry, crash reporting, or usage tracking of any kind. We do not know how many users install the app, how often it is opened, or what features are used. This is intentional: it is a privacy feature, not a limitation.

storage.title: Local Storage
storage.content: All processing happens on your Mac. Meeting audio and transcripts remain local to your system unless you explicitly share them. CloakView does not backup, sync, or upload any data to cloud storage.

thirdParties.title: Third Parties
thirdParties.content: CloakView does not share your data with third parties. The only external service is OpenAI's API, which you invoke directly with your own key. We do not have access to, control over, or visibility into OpenAI's processing of your data beyond their published privacy policy.

dataRights.title: Your Rights
dataRights.content:
Because we collect no data, there is nothing for us to provide, correct, or delete. Your data remains entirely on your device and under your control.

If you believe OpenAI has retained data incorrectly, you may contact OpenAI directly. CloakView has no involvement.

appUpdates.title: App Updates
appUpdates.content: The app does not automatically check for or download updates. You control when and whether to update CloakView by visiting the GitHub Releases page.

• Keeping your key confidential and secure.

CloakView operates as instructed with your key and does not monitor or restrict your usage.

overview.title: No Cookies or Tracking
overview.content:
CloakView does not use cookies, web beacons, pixels, or any other tracking technology. Our website and app do not store persistent identifiers or track your behavior.

This is not a limitation — it is a feature of our privacy-first design.

whyNo.title: Why No Analytics?
whyNo.content:
We believe your privacy should be the default, not an option. CloakView does not collect:
• How many users install the app.
• Which features are used most often.
• Crash reports or error telemetry.
• Session duration or app engagement.
• Geographic location or device information.
• Unique device identifiers.

This means we cannot easily measure adoption or debug issues with aggregate data, but it also means we cannot build surveillance into CloakView.

websiteCookies.title: This Website
websiteCookies.content: This website (getcloakview.com) does not use cookies, tracking scripts, or analytics tools. Visit our pages anonymously with full privacy.

thirdPartyScripts.title: No Third-Party Scripts
thirdPartyScripts.content: The CloakView website contains no Google Analytics, Segment, Mixpanel, or other telemetry services. No JavaScript is loaded from tracking domains.

localStorage.title: App Storage
localStorage.content: The CloakView app may store settings locally (such as your OpenAI API key in Keychain, or your preference for language or shortcuts) entirely on your Mac. No data is synced to cloud servers.

ifWeChange.title: If We Add Analytics
ifWeChange.content:
If CloakView ever adds telemetry, crash reporting, or analytics in the future:
• It will be opt-in, never forced.
• This policy will be updated and clearly published.
• You will be able to disable it at any time without affecting the app's core functionality.
• Current v1 releases will remain free of tracking.
